testerNotes.grantStacking: The gotchas doc's `export`-shadowing function relies on calling `grant_release` after every call; a skipped release leaves the lock set and every later call keeps a stale grant (`jj git push` 403s with 'could not read Username'). A burst-detecting variant needs no release: it adopts the first `export LEGION_GRANT` after a >=2s gap since the previous one. Source this once: export() { case "$1" in LEGION_GRANT=*) local now=$EPOCHSECONDS; if [ -z "${_lg_last:-}" ] || [ $((now - _lg_last)) -ge 2 ]; then LEGION_GRANT="${1#LEGION_GRANT=}"; builtin export LEGION_GRANT; fi; _lg_last=$now ;; *) builtin export "$@" ;; esac; }. Kept at /tmp/legion16-grant-trap.sh on this box.

testerNotes.testerScenarioOnThisBox: Follow .legion/plan.json testerScenario.steps. Concretely: (1) `legion state --json | jq .controllerLocator` — expect tmuxSession/tmuxWindowId/tmuxPaneId/ompSessionFile and no socketPath/runtime fields from this branch; `tmux -L legion-<slug> capture-pane -p -t <paneId>` shows the OMP prompt; `pstree -a $(tmux -L legion-<slug> list-panes -t <paneId> -F '#{pane_pid}')` shows omp with no `--mode rpc`/`worker-shim`; `tmux ... send-keys -t <paneId> 'What project are you the controller for?' Enter`. (2) Resume: kill-pane, then wake the controller (create a Dispatch issue in SMOKE_PROJECT or POST /v1/messages/publish to notifications.role.legion-<slug>-controller on the listener); daemon log line is `[legion] resurrecting the controller legion-<slug>-controller by resuming OMP session <file>` and the new pane command carries `--resume=<file>`. Fresh start logs `[legion] starting the controller fresh: no OMP session file is recorded`. (3) READY shape the controller expects: first line `READY #<n> at <sha> for <KEY> (<pr url>)`, then the PR body's gate facts. The controller finds the architect topic via `legion state --json` issues[KEY].parent chain. It publishes NOTHING after a successful merge; `pr-merged` on the architect topic comes from the daemon's webhook reducer. (4) Negative CLI control from any phase-worker pane: `legion gh -- pr merge <n> --squash` → exit 1, message `this grant cannot merge; publish READY to the controller: Only the controller may merge; publish READY to the controller`; daemon log shows the 403 on /legion/v1/gh-token; gh never spawned. testerNotes.rebaseRecipeIfLegion21LandsFirst: From the LEGION-16 architect (2026-09-12T07:21Z), relayed from LEGION-21's architect. LEGION-21 (runtime boundary) is PR #962 https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/962, already pushed at state v24 and in its testing phase, so it will most likely merge before #961. Its migrations are independent of ours but the CODE is not: on that branch the controller's spawn, stop, and probe no longer live in processes.ts. spawnController there only builds the environment and inner command and calls runtime.spawn("controller", spec); the tmux-specific controller branch in a new file, runtime-tmux.ts (TmuxRuntime.spawn), is what does prepareSocket, the worker-shim wrapping, and openWindow; markControllerReady reaches the socket through ProcessManager.clientFor -> runtime.connect(locator), which throws 'tmux locator <window> has no shim socket' when socketPath is absent (caught and logged). Recipe once #962 is on main (check with `legion gh -- pr view 962 --json state,mergedAt`): (1) rebase legion/LEGION-16 onto main; (2) our 'controller is not shimmed' change moves into runtime-tmux.ts's controller branch and to the connect/stop call sites, not the old processes.ts sites; markControllerReady and clientFor's controller path go away as before; the pane-kill stop path is whatever their runtime's stop branch is when no socket exists; (3) keep their shared Locator union (a z.discriminatedUnion on a `runtime` field; the tmux member already has tmuxPaneId and socketPath optional, so a controller locator without socketPath already parses) instead of a separate controller schema; their api/state.ts redactLocator already strips socketPath from every projected locator, so T3's state.ts step reduces to carrying ompSessionFile through; (4) renumber our migration to migrateV24State (v24 -> v25) and re-fixture its test: it strips socketPath and leaves their runtime field intact; (5) their branch adds a daemon/plugin version handshake — LEGION_DAEMON_API_VERSION in packages/contracts/src/legion-daemon-api.ts and legion.daemonApiVersion in packages/pi-envoy/package.json must be bumped together whenever LegionDaemonApi's shape changes, or the daemon refuses to boot against the installed plugin. #961 changes that shape (controllerLocator gains ompSessionFile on /state, /controller/ready gains ompSessionFile, /grants gains the controller form, /gh-token and /git-credential gain merge), so bump both together in the same commit and say so in the PR body's opening paragraph in plain English: the installed pi-envoy plugin must be released at the matching version before a daemon built from this change will boot. A rebase after review changes the head and the issue goes back through tester and reviewer; that is expected, not a defect. #962 had NOT merged when this handoff was written; whichever of tester, reviewer, or the implementer-again is active when it lands performs this recipe.

f1.cause: The controller's `state.roles[controllerToken]` claim, written by `/controller/ready`, was never deleted by anything (only worker paths delete claims; identical on main). `retireAndRespawnStuckController` returns at `if (this.deps.state.roles[token]) return;` and `ensureController`'s alive branch cancels the deadline on the same test, so after a daemon's first controller registration every later incarnation's deadline saw a claim (the predecessor's) and did nothing: a resumed pane that died during boot was recovered only by the next resync probe (~2.5 min on the rig), and a resumed pane that hung alive would never have been recovered.
f1.fixShape: (a) — `spawnController` deletes the previous incarnation's `state.roles[controllerToken]` claim alongside `delete controllerLocator`, after the resume decision has succeeded and before `mintControllerCapability`. The new pane puts the claim back through `/controller/ready`, the only path that writes it, so the guard keeps its meaning ('the current pane registered').
f1.whyNotB: (b) would compare the claim against a generation or session the deadline was armed for; the controller has neither a generation field nor a persisted expected session id, so (b) adds state to LegionState (another migration) for a comparison (a) makes unnecessary. (a) is one line and mirrors how `removeTreeWindow`/`retireWorkerLocator` already drop a claim when they retire a pane.
f1.claimConsumersChecked: Readers of the controller claim: `ensureController`'s alive branch and the deadline guard (the two this fixes), `index.ts` boot-time `controllerPendingNotices` drain (skips when no claim; `/controller/ready`'s `onControllerReady` drains them on the new pane's claim, so nothing is lost), `api/state.ts` redaction (projection only), and `/controller/ready` (the writer). Secret-file liveness (`liveSecretFiles`/`pruneSecretFiles`/`persist`) keys the controller's secret file off `controllerLocator`, never the claim, and `holdPaneSecret` covers the window between the locator delete and the fresh locator write — unchanged and still consistent with the route.
f1.takeoverInteraction: A `/legion-claim-controller` session's claim is also deleted when the daemon pane is respawned; before this fix the new pane's `/controller/ready` overwrote that claim anyway (and the Envoy role claim is last-claim-wins), so a respawn superseding a takeover is not new behaviour.
f1.tests: Two added to processes.test.ts beside the corrective-pass pair, both seeded with a registered first incarnation (`state.roles[controllerToken] = {role:"controller", sessionId:"ses-incarnation-1"}`) and its dead pane: (1) `resurrects a resumed controller whose pane died before re-claiming once the registration deadline fires, ignoring the previous incarnation's claim` — the resume of incarnation 2 leaves no claim, incarnation 2 dies during boot, the deadline fires, incarnation 3 is spawned with `--resume=<file>` and no kill-pane; (2) `kills a resumed controller pane that stays alive without re-claiming once the registration deadline fires, then resumes the same transcript` — incarnation 2 stays alive unclaimed, the deadline kills exactly pane %2, incarnation 3 is spawned with `--resume=<file>`. Both failed before the fix (stale claim survived; nothing killed) and pass after.
f1.docs: The daemon AGENTS.md controller bullet now states the claim deletion, that `/controller/ready` is the only writer, and that the deadline sentence holds 'whichever incarnation the pane is'.

secondRebase.interactionFinding: The role-claim bridge held one claim slot, last-bound instance wins. After the controller pane ran a task subagent (OMP binds a second envoyExtension in-process), the pane's /new re-claim executed in the subagent's envoy instance; the pane's instance had cleared its claimed topic on the /new rebind and heartbeated with nothing to re-assert, so main's heartbeat re-assertion never covered the controller after a session switch in a pane that had used a subagent. Fixed in commit 5ca28946: the bridge holds every bound instance with a live session-id reader, routes a claim to the instance serving the target session (last-bound on a tie, fallback to last-bound for an unserved session), removes an instance on session_shutdown; the regain re-run reads the pane's current session id and carries no transcript. The session-switch test models one SessionManager whose id /new mutates (as OMP does) and adds the heartbeat-after-switch-after-subagent case; it failed before the fix (5 s timeout, no /v1/roles read) and passes after. main's two regain tests were updated to this branch's boot shape (transcript reported at boot) and the transcript-free re-run.
